notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because none of the source pages loaded in a form I could read.

I tried to open six pages at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, and the NET Bible notes. The fetches came back in a format my code couldn't handle. When I tried to work out why, I'd used up the number of tool calls I'm allowed this turn, so I never read any of the content.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. With nothing read, I can't do that, and I didn't want to fill in Micah 6 from memory or attach URLs to things I haven't checked.

If you ask me to continue in a new message, I'll fetch the pages one at a time so a single error can't block the rest. This is the plan:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub and StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** this will probably centre on v. 8 (what "justice, mercy, humility" mean, and how they relate to the law and grace) and vv. 6–7 (sacrifice). I'll look at Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon, Desiring God, GTY, Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, 1517 and LCMS.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and New Advent (including the Church Fathers), Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'll also search for any well-known prosperity or hyper-grace use of v. 8 or vv. 14–15.
